intervention_label: Pending diagnostics that gate the ranked options (HLA class I typing, HA-1/HA-2 genotyping, quantitative CD33 and CD123, TP53 variant-level NGS with CNV, HLA-LOH on blasts)
regulatory_status: Laboratory testing rather than a regulated therapeutic. High-resolution HLA typing runs in ASHI-accredited histocompatibility laboratories; TP53 sequencing, p53 immunohistochemistry, 17p FISH and quantitative flow run in CLIA-certified clinical laboratories.

trials.title: HA-1 T TCR T Cell Immunotherapy after donor stem cell transplant
trials.indication: Relapsed/refractory acute leukaemia after allogeneic HCT
trials.notes: Listed here because HA-1 genotyping at rs1801284 is not a routine clinical send-out in the United States, and this protocol's screening pathway is the most reliable way to get both the patient and the sibling donor typed. Ask the intake team whether they perform it in-house during screening.

trials.title: Rezatapopt plus azacitidine in TP53 Y220C-mutant AML/MDS
trials.notes: Sets the standard the TP53 test has to meet: Y220C confirmed by CLIA-approved local testing at a variant allele frequency above 2%. That is the specification to hand the laboratory.

manufacturer.company: Not applicable; hospital and reference laboratories
manufacturer.notes: No manufacturer contact. The working contacts are the transplant centre's histocompatibility laboratory, the treating centre's flow cytometry laboratory, and the molecular pathology service that ran the 2019 and 2026 panels.

payer_access_notes: High-resolution HLA typing, TP53 sequencing, p53 immunohistochemistry, 17p FISH and diagnostic flow cytometry are routinely covered in a relapsed-leukaemia work-up. Quantitative antigen density and HA-1/HA-2 genotyping are the two that may not have a billing code and may need to run as research or trial-screening tests, which is an argument for routing them through a study team rather than the hospital order set.
access_summary: This is the cheapest and highest-yield item in the whole dossier, and most of it can be ordered today. The 2020 high-resolution HLA typing for both the patient and the sibling almost certainly exists in the first-transplant or donor-registry chart and needs retrieving rather than repeating, and A*02:01 status alone decides whether the HA-1 and CBX-250 routes are open at all. The exceptions are HA-1/HA-2 genotyping, which is not a routine US clinical send-out and is best obtained through the Fred Hutch screening pathway, and quantitative antigen density, which the flow laboratory has to be asked for by name.
next_steps: Request the 2020 high-resolution HLA typing reports for the patient and the sibling donor from the transplant centre or donor registry before ordering any new test; retrieval is faster than repeat typing and A*02:01 gates two of the best options

Ask the Fred Hutch intake line (206-606-4668 / immunotherapy@fredhutch.org) whether HA-1 rs1801284 and HA-2 genotyping for both the patient and the sibling can be run through NCT03326921 screening, since routine clinical laboratories generally do not offer it

Order quantitative CD33 and CD123 antigen density by name (antibodies bound per cell against calibrated beads, not mean fluorescence intensity), because qualitative positivity does not support ADC or engager selection

Order TP53 sequencing that reports the specific amino-acid change with variant allele frequency and includes copy-number calling, and add p53 immunohistochemistry and 17p FISH; retrieve the 2019 variant identity and allele frequency at the same time so the 2019-versus-2026 discrepancy is resolved on data

Discuss HLA-LOH testing with the transplant team before ordering it: genomic HLA haplotype loss requires a mismatched haplotype, so after an HLA-identical sibling graft the more informative question is HLA class I and class II downregulation on the blasts, which a flow or expression assay answers
geographic_scope: Available at the treating centre and its reference laboratories, with HA-1/HA-2 genotyping most reliably obtained through the Fred Hutch protocol in Seattle.

intervention_label: HA-1 TCR-T (donor-derived CD8+/CD4+ memory T cells, Bleakley/HighPassBio platform)
regulatory_status: investigational; IND-stage, no FDA or EMA filing

trials.title: HA-1 T TCR T Cell Immunotherapy for the Treatment of Patients With Relapsed or Refractory Acute Leukemia After Donor Stem Cell Transplant
trials.indication: Relapsed/refractory acute leukemia or MDS after allogeneic HCT
trials.notes: Single site, Fred Hutchinson Cancer Center, Seattle. Registry record last updated 2026-05-18, estimated completion 2028-07-16. A second registry phone is listed for the same contact: 855-557-0555. Protocol requires prior or ongoing allogeneic HCT rather than excluding it, sets no marrow-blast ceiling (>=5% blasts qualifies) and no performance-status floor, and allows other anti-leukemia treatment while on protocol. Three gates decide eligibility: recipient HLA-A*02:01 positive, recipient HA-1(H) genotype rs1801284 A/G or A/A, and the donor either HA-1(H)-negative (G/G) or HLA-A*02:01-negative. The product is made from donor cells, so the sibling donor has to be willing to give a fresh collection.

manufacturer.company: Fred Hutchinson Cancer Center (sponsor-investigator); HA-1 TCR originated with Marie Bleakley at Fred Hutch and was licensed to HighPassBio, an ElevateBio company
manufacturer.notes: No commercial medical-information line exists for this product. Cell manufacture and supply sit with the Fred Hutch program, so the trial intake line is the only route in.

payer_access_notes: Trial-supplied cell product; the sponsor covers the investigational agent. Routine care costs, lymphodepletion, donor collection and travel to Seattle are billed to the patient's insurer, and out-of-network authorisation for a Washington-state referral is the usual friction point.
access_summary: The Fred Hutch phase 1 is the one HA-1-directed program written for a patient like this one: prior allo-HCT is required, not excluded, and 85% marrow blasts does not disqualify. Everything now turns on genotyping, since the recipient must be HLA-A*02:01 positive and HA-1(H) positive while the sibling donor must be HA-1(H)-negative or A*02:01-negative. There is no off-trial route to this product.
next_steps: Call or email the Fred Hutch immunotherapy intake line (206-606-4668 / immunotherapy@fredhutch.org, NCT03326921) and ask what they need to open a screening file, including whether they will run the HA-1 rs1801284 genotyping in-house for both the patient and the sibling donor

Retrieve the 2020 high-resolution HLA typing for the patient and the sibling from the first-transplant / donor-registry chart before the call, since A*02:01 status decides whether the referral is worth making
Confirm with the sibling donor that a repeat apheresis collection is acceptable to her, because the product is donor-derived
Ask the study team about current slot availability and expected screening-to-infusion interval, and whether bridging cytoreduction on another protocol is permitted in the interval
Have the referring centre start out-of-network / travel authorisation in parallel rather than after eligibility is confirmed
geographic_scope: United States; single open site (Seattle, WA). Unrelated donors residing outside the US are handled through NMDP-affiliated centres, which does not apply to an HLA-identical sibling.

intervention_label: HA-1 / HA-2 minor-histocompatibility-antigen TCR-T (class review, incl. TSC-100/TSC-101 and BSB-1001)
regulatory_status: investigational; no FDA or EMA filing for any agent in the class

trials.title: Study of TSC-100 and TSC-101 in Patients With Hematologic Malignancies Undergoing Allogeneic HCT
trials.notes: Exclusion criteria list prior allogeneic HCT outright, and the design enrolls patients preparing for a haploidentical, MMUD or MUD transplant. A late relapse six years after a matched-sibling allograft is outside the protocol in two directions at once. 21 US sites, recruiting as of the 2026-07-21 registry update.

trials.title: BSB-1001 in Patients Undergoing HLA-Matched Allogeneic Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplant
trials.central_contact_name: Medical Director: Nawazish Khan, MD, BlueSphere Bio
trials.notes: Two independent bars: prior allogeneic transplantation is an exclusion, and marrow blasts must be no higher than 25%. Requires HLA-A*02:01 plus HA-1 positivity. 6 US sites.

trials.title: MDG1021 (HA-1H TCR-modified donor T cells)
trials.notes: Withdrawn before enrolling; the registry reason reads 'Medigene transfered all rights to a new Sponsor'. Medigene AG entered insolvency proceedings in 2025, so this Leiden-based HA-1 program has no live sponsor.

manufacturer.notes: TScan's published expanded-access policy states it does not provide access to investigational products outside clinical trials, and directs provider questions to medicalaffairs@tscan.com. BlueSphere Bio publishes no expanded-access policy; the registry medical-director contact is the only route.

access_summary: Every commercial HA-1/HA-2 TCR-T program is built around a first transplant and excludes patients who have already had an allograft, which this patient had in 2020. TScan states it does not supply outside trials, so there is no compassionate-use fallback either. The HA-directed idea stays alive for her only through the Fred Hutch protocol (NCT03326921), which requires prior allo-HCT.
next_steps: Treat the TScan and BlueSphere programs as closed for this patient and put the effort into NCT03326921 instead
If the treating team wants the exclusion confirmed in writing, email medicalaffairs@tscan.com quoting NCT05473910 and the prior matched-sibling allograft
Ask BlueSphere (nkhan@bluespherebio.com) whether any post-transplant-relapse cohort of BSB-1001 is planned, and log the answer for a future re-screen
Re-screen this class if the patient proceeds to a second allograft, since a first-transplant-conditioned design could become relevant to a subsequent donor pairing
geographic_scope: United States (both programs); no EU sites listed.

intervention_label: CBX-250 (CG1/HLA-A*02:01 x CD3 TCR-mimetic bispecific T-cell engager)
regulatory_status: investigational; phase 1, no filing

trials.title: CBX-250 in relapsed/refractory myeloid leukaemias (CROSSCHECK-001)
trials.notes: The protocol says relapse at any time after HSCT is eligible, which is unusual and directly useful here. Gates: documented HLA-A*02:01 positivity, white cells below 25,000 at enrollment (cytoreduction permitted, hydroxyurea allowed concurrently with sponsor approval), ECOG 0-1, at least 60 days from HSCT and 4 weeks from any donor lymphocyte infusion. Eleven US sites including City of Hope, Stanford, Moffitt, Northwestern, Dana-Farber, Washington University, MSKCC and Thomas Jefferson. Registry updated 2026-03-16.

manufacturer.notes: Crossbow publishes a compassionate-use policy stating that physicians interested in treating a patient with CBX-250 should complete the request form and send it to clinical@crossbowtx.com. That gives this agent something most phase 1 programmes in this dossier lack: a named route for a patient who cannot enrol.

payer_access_notes: Sponsor-supplied agent inside the trial. A compassionate-use supply would still leave the patient's insurer covering administration, monitoring and cytokine-release management.
access_summary: Of the HLA-A*02:01-restricted options, this is the one with the widest geographic footprint and the most permissive post-transplant language, and it also has a published compassionate-use address if a slot is not available. The single decisive gate is HLA-A*02:01 status, the same value that governs the HA-1 pathway. White cells need to be under 25,000 at enrollment, which cytoreduction can address.
next_steps: Retrieve HLA-A*02:01 status first; without it neither this nor the HA-1 route can be screened

Email Rachel Ghiraldi (rachel.ghiraldi@crossbowtx.com, 857-301-6432, NCT06994676) to ask which of the eleven sites has open slots and what cytoreduction they accept to reach a white count under 25,000
Ask whether CG1 (cathepsin G) expression is measured on study or whether HLA-A*02:01 positivity alone qualifies, so the workup list is complete
If no slot is available, have the treating physician request the compassionate-use form at clinical@crossbowtx.com and submit it alongside the trial enquiry rather than after it
Note the ECOG 0-1 requirement and keep performance status documented, since it can drift quickly at this disease burden
geographic_scope: United States; eleven listed sites across CA, FL, IL, MA, MO, NY and PA.

intervention_label: WT1-TCRC4 CD8+ T cells (TTCR-C4, HLA-A*02:01-restricted), prophylactic post-HCT
regulatory_status: investigational; no FDA or EMA filing

trials.title: WT1-TCRc4 gene-transduced CD8+ Tcm transferred after allogeneic HCT
trials.notes: Terminated for slow accrual; the registry gives a 2020-03-20 completion and no successor arm under this protocol.

trials.title: FH-WT1-E50 TCR T Cells With Azacitidine for Measurable Residual Disease in AML
trials.notes: The current Fred Hutch WT1 program, and the closest thing to a successor. It excludes prior allogeneic HCT at leukapheresis and requires morphologic remission with MRD only, so 85% marrow blasts fails it twice over.

manufacturer.notes: Academic program with no commercial sponsor and no medical-information line.

access_summary: The original WT1-TCRc4 protocol closed for slow accrual and nothing replaced it for post-transplant relapse. The live Fred Hutch WT1 successor treats MRD in first remission and excludes patients with a prior allograft, so neither protocol is open to this patient. WT1 stays a target of interest only if a future study accepts post-HCT relapse.
next_steps: Skip WT1-directed TCR-T for now; the same Fred Hutch intake line (206-606-4668) already being used for NCT03326921 will flag any new WT1 cohort
Ask the intake team directly whether a post-allo-HCT relapse cohort of FH-WT1-E50 is planned, and record the answer with a date
Keep HLA-A*02:01 status on file, since it gates any future WT1 protocol as well as the HA-1 one
geographic_scope: United States; Seattle only.

intervention_label: WT1-siTCR gene-transduced lymphocytes (HLA-A*24:02-restricted; logged upstream as TBI-1301)

trials.title: Gene-modified WT1 TCR T cells (Cell Medica)
trials.notes: UK study, completed 2018; Cell Medica no longer develops it.

Takara's active siTCR clinical work is the NY-ESO-1 product (mipetresgene autoleucel), for which a new Japanese confirmatory trial notification cleared PMDA review in September 2025; that is a different antigen and a different indication.

access_summary: The WT1-siTCR platform sits with Japanese investigators and has no open study a US patient could enter, so this is a geography-and-sponsor problem rather than a biology one. It only becomes a question at all if the patient turns out to be HLA-A*02:01-negative and A*24:02-positive. Even then the route would be an investigator-initiated Japanese protocol.
next_steps: Resolve HLA-A*24:02 alongside A*02:01 in the same typing pull, so this branch is either opened or closed on data
If A*02:01-negative and A*24:02-positive, ask the treating haematologist to write to the Mie University group about any enrolling WT1-siTCR study before assuming there is one

Confirm the product designation before any outreach: upstream files carry this as TBI-1301, which is Takara's NY-ESO-1 siTCR product, so the WT1 program identifier should be checked against the sponsor's own materials
geographic_scope: Japan; no US, EU or AU site for the WT1 product.
notes: Possible upstream naming drift: TBI-1301 is Takara's NY-ESO-1 siTCR product (mipetresgene autoleucel), while the WT1 siTCR program has been reported under a separate designation. Flagged rather than corrected, since trials.jsonl and the evidence files are not mine to edit.

regulatory_status: investigational; development stopped, no filing

trials.notes: Terminated on a company decision; Bellicum no longer develops the program.

manufacturer.notes: The Munich local court opened insolvency proceedings over the assets of Medigene AG and Medigene Immunotherapies GmbH by order dated 1 August 2025, after the company had already shifted away from haematology and sought a partner for MDG1011. There is no sponsor to receive a compassionate-use request.

access_summary: Both PRAME TCR-T programs that reached patients are closed, and Medigene is in insolvency proceedings, so there is no sponsor left to ask. PRAME as a target is not dead, but no PRAME-directed cell product is obtainable for this patient today. Do not spend screening effort here.
next_steps: Record PRAME as unavailable rather than pending, so the board does not carry it as a live option
If PRAME expression is measured for other reasons, keep the result on file for any future PRAME-directed engager or TCR program
Re-screen only if a new sponsor announces a PRAME TCR-T study that accepts post-allo-HCT relapse

regulatory_status: investigational; no FDA or EMA filing

trials.title: MT-401-OTS (off-the-shelf multiTAA-specific T cells) in AML
trials.notes: Requires marrow blasts <=10% and peripheral blasts <=5% at screening, or MRD-level disease. Closed at 85% blasts, but reachable if a cytoreductive regimen produces a response. Sites: City of Hope, Moffitt, KU Cancer Center. A second registry contact is listed: Beth Lepping, BSN, elepping@markertherapeutics.com.

trials.title: Donor-derived multiTAA-specific T cells (ADSPAM)
trials.notes: Baylor College of Medicine; closed to new enrollment as of the 2025-10-21 update.

trials.title: Tumour-associated-antigen-specific T cells (TAA-T) after allogeneic HCT
trials.notes: Enrolls patients who have not had haematologic relapse and excludes anyone who has received or will receive a second allogeneic HCT. Both conditions cut against this case.

manufacturer.company: Marker Therapeutics (MT-401-OTS); Baylor College of Medicine and Children's National (academic programs)
manufacturer.notes: Marker publishes no separate expanded-access policy; the registry study contacts are the working route.

payer_access_notes: Investigational cell products are sponsor-supplied. The cost exposure is standard-of-care bridging therapy and travel, not the agent.
access_summary: Multi-antigen T-cell products are all gated on low disease burden, and at 85% marrow blasts none of the three studies will take her now. MT-401-OTS is the one worth tracking, because it becomes reachable if a salvage regimen drops marrow blasts to 10% or less. The other two are either closed to enrollment or written for patients who have not relapsed.
next_steps: Email Marker Therapeutics (pallison@markertherapeutics.com, NCT06552416) now to ask how quickly they can screen a patient who reaches <=10% marrow blasts on salvage, so the window is not missed later
Sequence this behind whatever cytoreductive option the board picks; it is a consolidation-slot candidate, not an induction one
Ask whether the off-the-shelf product requires any HLA restriction the patient must be typed for, and fold that into the same typing request
Re-check NCT02494167 status in three months in case Baylor reopens accrual
geographic_scope: United States; MT-401-OTS at City of Hope, Moffitt and KU Cancer Center.

intervention_label: GLIDE (guided lymphocyte immunopeptide-derived expansion; donor anti-leukaemia T cells)

The registry lists extension 6247 for this contact and a second contact, Stéphanie Thiant, PhD, at extension 4681 (sthiant.hmr@ssss.gouv.qc.ca).

One phone call would settle it, but nothing here should be planned around it. Note the site is in Montreal, so a Canadian referral would be needed even if it were live.
next_steps: If anyone wants this closed definitively, call (514) 252-3400 extension 6247 or email jgnemorin@centrec3i.com and ask whether the protocol is still open
Otherwise treat GLIDE as dormant and do not carry it into the ranking as a live option
Note the Canadian location, which would require a cross-border referral even in the best case

intervention_label: Tagraxofusp (SL-401, CD123-directed diphtheria-toxin fusion protein)
regulatory_status: FDA-approved (ELZONRIS, blastic plasmacytoid dendritic cell neoplasm, adults and paediatric patients 2 years and older, 2018); EMA-approved for BPDCN. No AML indication.

trials.title: SL-401 in Combination With Azacitidine or Azacitidine/Venetoclax in AML and MDS
trials.notes: Requires locally determined CD123/IL3RA expression within 3 months of first treatment, which the pending quantitative CD123 flow would satisfy. Excludes HSCT within 60 days of screening and active GVHD, neither of which applies six years out. Sites: Dana-Farber, City of Hope, MD Anderson. Second registry contact: Veronica Zehnder, veronica_zehnder@dfci.harvard.edu. Note the venetoclax-containing arms sit against documented venetoclax refractoriness.

trials.title: Tagraxofusp and Azacitidine for Maintenance Treatment in CD123-Positive AML/MDS after allogeneic HCT
trials.notes: Written for first or second allogeneic HCT, so it becomes relevant only if the patient proceeds to HCT2. Excludes anti-CD123 therapy given after the transplant, which constrains sequencing if a CD123 agent is used earlier. Single site, City of Hope.

trials.title: Tagraxofusp and Low-Intensity Chemotherapy for CD123-Positive Relapsed or Refractory AML
trials.notes: Excludes any prior therapy other than venetoclax plus a hypomethylating agent (with IDH/FLT3 inhibitors allowed after). FLAG-IDA and a prior allograft put this patient outside that window. Single site, Stanford.

manufacturer.company: Stemline Therapeutics, a Menarini Group company
manufacturer.notes: 1-877-332-7961 is the number published for medical information and for reporting adverse events, staffed Monday to Friday 8:30 am to 5:30 pm ET. The grants@menarinistemline.com address on the same site is for grants and sponsorships, not medical enquiries.

payer_access_notes: Off-label in AML. US payers generally hold tagraxofusp to its BPDCN label, so an AML request goes through off-label prior authorisation without an NCCN AML listing behind it; expect to argue it. Enrolling on NCT03113643 sidesteps the coverage question entirely because the drug is supplied.
access_summary: Tagraxofusp is an approved drug, so a treating team can prescribe it off-label for CD123-positive AML without waiting for a trial slot, but reimbursement is the obstacle rather than supply. The cleaner route is the Dana-Farber/City of Hope/MD Anderson study, which takes CD123-positive R/R AML and only needs a local CD123 result. Quantitative CD123 density strengthens either route.
next_steps: Email Andrew Lane's team at Dana-Farber (andrew_lane@dfci.harvard.edu, NCT03113643) with the CD123 flow result and ask which arm is open, given documented venetoclax refractoriness
Order the quantitative CD123 antigen-density flow now; the trial needs a CD123 result within 3 months of first dose and an off-label appeal reads better with density than with a bare 'positive'
If the trial route stalls, call Stemline medical information at 1-877-332-7961 for the off-label dossier and have the payer team open a prior-authorisation file early
Keep NCT06498973 in reserve as post-HCT2 maintenance, and note its exclusion of post-transplant anti-CD123 therapy when sequencing CD123 agents
Flag capillary leak syndrome monitoring requirements to the treating centre before committing, since they shape which site can deliver it
geographic_scope: United States for both the approved product and the open studies; approved in the EU for BPDCN.

intervention_label: Pivekimab sunirine (IMGN632, CD123-directed antibody-drug conjugate)
regulatory_status: FDA-approved 27 May 2026 as DECNUPAZ (pivekimab sunirine-pvzy) for adults with blastic plasmacytoid dendritic cell neoplasm; boxed warning for hepatotoxicity including hepatic veno-occlusive disease. No AML indication.

trials.title: Pivekimab sunirine with or without venetoclax and/or azacitidine in AML
trials.notes: Closed to new enrollment as of the 2025-08-14 registry update; 29 sites.

trials.title: Pivekimab sunirine in CD123-positive haematologic malignancies
trials.notes: The CADENZA/first-in-human program; closed to new enrollment, 28 sites.

trials.title: Pivekimab sunirine plus venetoclax and azacitidine versus placebo plus venetoclax and azacitidine in AML
trials.notes: Front-line design; a patient refractory to FLAG-IDA plus venetoclax after an allograft is outside it. Listed here so the user can see the only recruiting adult AML pivekimab study and why it does not fit.

manufacturer.notes: 844-663-3742 reaches AbbVie medical information (Monday to Friday, 8:00 am to 5:30 pm CT) and is also the number the AbbVie call centre uses on its trial listings. Because the drug is now approved, an AML request is an off-label prescription question rather than a pre-approval-access one; AbbVie's pre-approval policy explicitly does not apply to patients eligible for an ongoing trial.

payer_access_notes: Newly approved for BPDCN, so an AML use is off-label against a 2026 label with a boxed hepatotoxicity warning. Prior authorisation should be expected to be contested, and the veno-occlusive-disease signal matters more than usual in a patient heading toward a second transplant.
access_summary: The BPDCN approval in May 2026 turned pivekimab from a trial-only agent into a drug a treating team can write off-label for CD123-positive AML. Both adult AML studies that took relapsed/refractory patients are closed to new enrollment, and the one recruiting adult study is front-line, so the trial door is effectively shut. The real constraints are payer authorisation and the hepatic veno-occlusive-disease warning ahead of any second allograft.
next_steps: Call AbbVie medical information at 844-663-3742 to confirm current off-label supply logistics and to ask whether any AML cohort is reopening
Have the transplant team weigh the boxed hepatic veno-occlusive-disease warning against a planned second allo-HCT before the drug is requested, since sequencing is the safety question here
Pair the request with quantitative CD123 antigen density rather than qualitative positivity
Open the off-label prior-authorisation file early and expect to appeal
geographic_scope: United States (FDA approval, May 2026); no equivalent EU approval identified at this check.

intervention_label: VIP943 (CD123-directed antibody-drug conjugate)
regulatory_status: investigational; phase 1, no filing. Sponsor initiated wind-down activities in 2025.

Vincerx terminated its Oqory reverse-merger term sheet on 2025-02-28 with roughly $3.9M in cash, subsequently terminated a further merger letter of intent, and its board authorised management to begin wind-down activities while exploring out-licensing. Reporting this as cleanly recruiting would be wrong. The honest position is that VIP943 is unavailable unless a site says otherwise on the phone.
next_steps: Call one of the named US sites rather than the sponsor first: MD Anderson or Fred Hutch can say in one call whether the VIP943 slot is physically open
Try clinicaltrials@vincerx.com / 16508006676 as captured from the registry, understanding that the line may not be staffed
If a site confirms closure, treat CD123 targeting through tagraxofusp or pivekimab instead
Watch for an out-licensing announcement, which would be the only route by which this asset returns

intervention_label: CD123-directed CAR T cells and switchable CD123 CAR platforms
regulatory_status: investigational; no approved CD123 CAR product

trials.title: Allo-RevCAR01-T with the R-TM123 CD123 target module in CD123-positive haematologic malignancies
trials.notes: Eleven German sites. Two hard bars for this patient: marrow blasts must be at or below 30% (30-40% only on two consecutive assessments), and allogeneic transplantation within the last 2 months or GVHD on systemic immunosuppression excludes. At roughly 85% marrow blasts she is outside the blast criterion, and the record states that exceptions to minimum CD123 expression are not allowed. A second registry contact is listed: Martina Raupach, same email and phone.

trials.title: CLL-1 / CD33 / CD123-directed CAR-T
trials.notes: Single site in Shenzhen, China.

manufacturer.company: AvenCell Europe GmbH (Allo-RevCAR01-T); Shenzhen Geno-Immune Medical Institute
manufacturer.notes: The AvenCell address published on the registry record is study-specific rather than a general medical-information desk. No expanded-access policy identified for either sponsor.

payer_access_notes: Both routes sit outside US coverage. On the German study the agent is sponsor-supplied but everything around it, including travel and any bridging therapy, falls outside a US plan's network.
access_summary: The switchable CD123 CAR platform is the most interesting of the CD123 cell therapies because the target module can be switched off if toxicity develops, but its blast ceiling of about 30% puts it out of reach at 85% marrow blasts. It is also Germany-only. If a cytoreductive regimen produces a real response, this becomes worth a second look; until then it is closed on disease burden as much as on geography.
next_steps: Confirm a reachable site before planning anything: at this check the CD123 CAR options are Germany and mainland China only, with no US site
If salvage brings marrow blasts under 30%, email AVC-201-01@avencell.com to ask whether a US-resident patient can be screened at a German site and what the residency and follow-up requirements are
Order quantitative CD123 antigen density, since the AvenCell protocol states that exceptions to minimum CD123 expression are not permitted
Prefer reachable CD123 agents (tagraxofusp, pivekimab) for cytoreduction rather than holding a slot open for a CAR that cannot enroll her today
geographic_scope: Germany (11 sites) and mainland China (1 site). No US, UK or AU site identified.

intervention_label: Flotetuzumab (MGD006, CD123 x CD3 DART)
regulatory_status: investigational; development discontinued, no filing

trials.title: Flotetuzumab in AML and MDS
trials.notes: Terminated on a business decision; 43 sites closed.

trials.title: Flotetuzumab Expanded Access Program
trials.notes: MacroGenics ran a formal expanded-access protocol and it is listed as no longer available, so even the compassionate route is shut.

manufacturer.notes: No medical-information line captured for a discontinued programme; the company's registry study director listing is historical.

access_summary: MacroGenics stopped flotetuzumab on a business decision and then closed its expanded-access protocol, so both the trial and the compassionate routes are gone. The CD123 x CD3 engager idea survives in other molecules, not in this one. No action is available here.
next_steps: Record flotetuzumab as closed so it is not re-raised at board
Carry the CD123 engager rationale into agents that still have a sponsor rather than pursuing this molecule
geographic_scope: No open access path in any geography.

intervention_label: Vibecotamab (XmAb14045, CD123 x CD3 bispecific)
regulatory_status: investigational; active development ended, no filing

trials.title: Vibecotamab in MDS or CMML after hypomethylating agent failure and in MRD-positive AML
trials.notes: MD Anderson terminated the study, registry completion 2026-05-15, reason recorded as under 75% participation.

manufacturer.notes: Novartis returned ex-US rights and Xencor did not carry the molecule forward, so there is no sponsor supplying it. No medical-information line captured for a shelved programme.

access_summary: Vibecotamab has no sponsor advancing it and the last academic study closed in May 2026. There is no trial, no expanded-access protocol and no marketed product to prescribe. Treat it as a closed line of enquiry.
next_steps: Record vibecotamab as closed
If a CD123 x CD3 engager is wanted, direct the question to sponsors with live programmes rather than to Xencor
geographic_scope: No open access path in any geography.

intervention_label: Fractionated gemtuzumab ozogamicin (CD33-directed antibody-drug conjugate)
regulatory_status: FDA-approved (MYLOTARG). The label carries two indications: newly-diagnosed CD33-positive AML in adults and paediatric patients 1 month and older, and relapsed or refractory CD33-positive AML in adults and paediatric patients 2 years and older. EMA-approved for newly-diagnosed CD33-positive AML.

trials.title: CLAG-GO (cladribine, cytarabine, G-CSF plus fractionated gemtuzumab ozogamicin) in AML
trials.notes: Explicitly allows patients who relapse after allogeneic HCT, provided they are at least 60 days from stem-cell infusion, have no more than grade 1 GVHD and are off all immunosuppression. Requires relapse after or refractoriness to at least one intensive regimen, which FLAG-IDA satisfies. Symptomatic leukostasis excludes, and G-CSF is part of the regimen, so a rising peripheral blast count needs discussing before screening. Single site, University of Maryland, Baltimore. Second registry contact: Oyinkansola Arasanmi, 410-328-6635, Oyinkansola.Arasanmi@umm.edu.

manufacturer.notes: Pfizer medical information is staffed 9 am to 5 pm ET Monday to Friday, with online chat and a written-enquiry form on the same site. Pfizer's historic gemtuzumab expanded-access protocol (NCT02312037) is listed as no longer available, which no longer matters now that the product is marketed.

payer_access_notes: This is the unusual case in the dossier where the label already covers the patient's situation: relapsed or refractory CD33-positive AML in an adult. That makes it an on-label Part B buy-and-bill prescription rather than an off-label appeal. Pfizer Oncology Together patient support is reachable at 1-877-744-5675, Monday to Friday 8 am to 8 pm ET.
access_summary: Gemtuzumab ozogamicin is on-label for exactly this patient's situation, relapsed or refractory CD33-positive AML in an adult, so her own team can prescribe it without a trial slot or an off-label appeal. The open question is antigen density rather than access, since qualitative CD33 positivity does not predict benefit the way antibodies-bound-per-cell does. The CLAG-GO study at Maryland offers the same drug inside a salvage backbone and is the one strong-fit trial in the dossier.
next_steps: Order quantitative CD33 antigen-density flow before committing, since it is the variable that separates a reasonable ADC bet from a futile one

Contact the University of Maryland study team (veronica.kflu@umm.edu / 410-328-9416, NCT04050280) about a screening slot, and ask how they handle a rapidly rising peripheral blast count given the G-CSF priming
If the trial route is slow, have the treating haematologist write fractionated single-agent gemtuzumab on-label as a bridge and confirm the Part B billing pathway locally
Document hepatic function and any veno-occlusive-disease risk factors ahead of a possible second transplant, because sinusoidal obstruction syndrome is the sequencing risk
Ask Pfizer medical information (1-800-438-1985) for the fractionated MyloFrance-style dosing dossier if the local team wants it
geographic_scope: United States and EU for the marketed product; the CLAG-GO study is single-site in Baltimore, Maryland.

intervention_label: CLAG-GO (cladribine, high-dose cytarabine, G-CSF plus fractionated gemtuzumab ozogamicin)
regulatory_status: Regimen of individually approved agents. Gemtuzumab ozogamicin is FDA-approved for relapsed/refractory CD33-positive AML; cladribine, cytarabine and filgrastim are approved products used off-label in this combination.

trials.title: CLAG-GO in AML
trials.notes: Registry record updated 2026-07-01, estimated completion 2028-02. Post-allograft relapse is explicitly eligible at >=60 days from infusion with no more than grade 1 GVHD and off immunosuppression. Excludes APL and CML blast phase. PI: Vu H. Duong, MD, MS.

manufacturer.company: University of Maryland, Baltimore (sponsor); Pfizer supplies gemtuzumab ozogamicin commercially
manufacturer.notes: Investigator-initiated regimen, so there is no single company to call. The only branded component with a medical-information desk is gemtuzumab ozogamicin (Pfizer).

payer_access_notes: Inside the trial, protocol-specified drug and monitoring are covered by the study. Off-trial, every component is a marketed product and gemtuzumab is on-label here, so the regimen can usually be assembled without a novel coverage fight, though the cladribine-based backbone itself is off-label combination use.
access_summary: This is the one strong-fit trial in the dossier and it takes post-allograft relapse by name. If the Maryland slot does not materialise, the regimen can be reproduced at the home centre from marketed drugs, which is the practical fallback that most other options in this case do not have. The gating items are the 60-day and GVHD conditions, both comfortably met six years out.
next_steps: Call the University of Maryland study contacts (410-328-9416 / veronica.kflu@umm.edu) this week and ask about slot availability and screening turnaround for NCT04050280
Send the marrow report, current blast trajectory and CD33 flow with the first contact so screening is not delayed
Confirm the patient is off all immunosuppression and has no more than grade 1 GVHD, and get that documented
Ask the home centre in parallel whether it will deliver CLAG plus fractionated gemtuzumab off-trial if the Baltimore slot slips
Plan the cellular or transplant consolidation before starting, since CLAG-GO is a cytoreduction step in a curative-intent sequence rather than an endpoint
geographic_scope: United States; single trial site in Baltimore, Maryland, with the regimen reproducible at any centre from marketed drugs.

intervention_label: BMS-986497 (ORM-6151, CD33-directed antibody-conjugated GSPT1 degrader)
regulatory_status: investigational; IND-stage, no filing

trials.title: BMS-986497 in relapsed/refractory AML and MDS
trials.central_contact_name: BMS Clinical Trials Contact Center www.BMSClinicalTrials.com
trials.notes: Published criteria are broad: adults with primary or secondary relapsed and/or refractory AML or MDS, detectable CD33 expression, failure of alternative therapies with established benefit, ECOG <=2 and adequate organ function. Prior allogeneic HCT is not listed as an exclusion in the public record, which needs confirming with the site rather than assumed. 16 listed sites with two withdrawn; registry updated 2026-04-08. BMS asks that the first line of any email contain the NCT number and site number.

manufacturer.notes: 1-800-321-1335 is the US medical information contact centre, Monday to Friday 8 am to 5 pm ET. BMS publishes pre-approval access and post-study access information through its healthcare-provider medical resources pages.

payer_access_notes: Investigational; drug supplied by the sponsor. Standard trial-participation cost rules apply.
access_summary: This is the broadest CD33-directed study open to her on paper: relapsed or refractory AML, any detectable CD33, ECOG up to 2, with prior allograft not named as an exclusion. Sixteen sites makes it geographically the easiest to reach of the CD33 options. The two things to confirm with a site are the post-transplant question and whether the current dose-escalation cohort is open.
next_steps: Email Clinical.Trials@bms.com with NCT06419634 in the first line, or call 855-907-3286, and ask which sites have open slots and whether prior allogeneic HCT is permitted
Ask for the full protocol exclusion list, since the public registry summary ends with 'other protocol-defined inclusion/exclusion criteria apply'
Send documented CD33 expression with the enquiry and add quantitative density when it returns
Check whether the marrow blast burden and any leukocytosis limits apply, as they are not in the public record
geographic_scope: United States; 16 listed sites, two withdrawn.

intervention_label: CD33-directed CAR T cells
regulatory_status: investigational; no approved CD33 CAR-T product

trials.title: Anti-CD33 CAR-T in relapsed/refractory AML
trials.notes: City of Hope, single site, registry updated 2026-03-05. Prior allogeneic transplant is allowed if more than 6 months out, and the protocol requires an identified stem-cell source for a subsequent allograft, specifying the original donor for a previously transplanted patient. That fits an HLA-identical sibling who is still available. No central contact is published on the registry record; the listed principal investigator is Karamjeet S Sandhu. Route the enquiry through City of Hope's clinical trials office rather than an invented direct line.

trials.title: CLL-1 / CD33 / CD123-directed CAR-T
trials.notes: Single site in Shenzhen, Guangdong, China. Requires confirmed CLL-1, CD123 and/or CD33 expression. Geography, manufacturing jurisdiction and post-infusion follow-up all sit in mainland China.

manufacturer.company: City of Hope Medical Center (sponsor, NCT05672147); Shenzhen Geno-Immune Medical Institute (sponsor, NCT04010877)
manufacturer.notes: Academic sponsors; no commercial medical-information line and no published expanded-access programme for either construct.

payer_access_notes: Cell product is supplied by the study. Lymphodepletion, apheresis, prolonged cytopenia management and the planned consolidative transplant are billed to the insurer, and CD33 CAR-T carries an expectation of marrow aplasia that makes the transplant backup non-optional.
access_summary: The City of Hope study is the realistic CD33 CAR-T route and it is written for a post-allograft patient with a donor still identifiable, which describes this case. On-target marrow aplasia means the protocol assumes a subsequent transplant, so it only makes sense as part of a transplant-consolidation plan. The Shenzhen study is open but mainland-China-only.
next_steps: Confirm a US site is reachable before pursuing the Chinese study: contact City of Hope's clinical trials office about NCT05672147 and ask them to confirm the current screening contact, since the registry record lists no central contact
Confirm the sibling donor's availability and willingness for a further collection, because the protocol requires the original donor as the stem-cell source
Order quantitative CD33 antigen density alongside the trial enquiry
Ask the study team how they sequence CD33 CAR-T against a planned second allograft, since the aplasia risk drives the timeline
Only revisit NCT04010877 if the US route closes, and then ask explicitly about non-resident enrollment and follow-up obligations in Shenzhen
geographic_scope: United States (City of Hope, Duarte CA) and mainland China (Shenzhen) only.

intervention_label: GTB-3650 (anti-CD16 / IL-15 / anti-CD33 tri-specific killer engager)
regulatory_status: investigational; no filing

trials.title: GTB-3650 TriKE in CD33-positive myeloid malignancies
trials.notes: Single site, Masonic Cancer Center, University of Minnesota; registry updated 2026-07-14. Two criteria to check carefully: peripheral blasts must be at or below 20,000 at treatment start, with hydroxyurea allowed to get there, and the patient must be a transplant candidate or newly relapsed after transplant with no post-transplant therapy given. This patient has had FLAG-IDA plus venetoclax since her relapse, so the second criterion needs a direct ruling from the study team.

manufacturer.company: GT Biopharma, Inc. (product); Masonic Cancer Center, University of Minnesota (sponsor)
manufacturer.notes: No manufacturer medical-information line captured. The academic sponsor's study contact is the working route.

payer_access_notes: Sponsor-supplied agent; a continuous-infusion schedule means an inpatient or infusion-centre commitment that should be confirmed with the site before travel is booked.
access_summary: A single-site phase 1 in Minneapolis with a live contact, but eligibility hinges on a clause that reads against this patient: transplant candidate, or newly relapsed after transplant with no post-transplant therapy given. Since she has already had FLAG-IDA plus venetoclax since relapsing, the study team has to rule on it rather than the file. Peripheral blasts also need to be under 20,000 at treatment start.
next_steps: Call or email Mark Juckett's team (612-624-9452 / juck0001@umn.edu, NCT06594445) and put the post-transplant-therapy question to them directly before anything else
Ask whether hydroxyurea-controlled blasts under 20,000 is acceptable given a peripheral blast fraction that reached 82%
Confirm the inpatient or infusion-schedule commitment and expected duration, since this is a travel-dependent option
Keep this behind CLAG-GO and the CD33 ADC routes unless the eligibility ruling comes back favourable
geographic_scope: United States; single site in Minneapolis, Minnesota.

intervention_label: Dual CD33/CD123-directed CAR T cells (Loop33 x 123 and related constructs)
regulatory_status: investigational; no approved dual-targeted CAR product

trials.title: CLL-1 / CD33 / CD123-directed CAR-T in relapsed/refractory AML
trials.notes: The only recruiting study covering simultaneous CD33 and CD123 targeting, and it runs at a single site in Shenzhen, Guangdong, China. Requires confirmed CLL-1, CD123 and/or CD33 expression by IHC or flow. Registry updated 2026-06-23 with completion estimated 2029-12-31.

manufacturer.notes: Academic institute; no published expanded-access route and no medical-information line identified. Correspondence contact is the principal investigator listed on the registry record.

payer_access_notes: US insurers do not cover care delivered on a Chinese academic protocol. Cell manufacture, hospitalisation and toxicity management would be self-funded, and the CAR-T toxicity window is not one to manage far from the treating team.
access_summary: Dual CD33/CD123 targeting exists in the clinic only through a single mainland-China study, so this is a geography problem before it is a biology problem. The dual-antigen rationale is strong for a patient whose blasts carry both antigens, but no US or EU site is running it. Both antigens can still be attacked sequentially with agents that are reachable.
next_steps: Confirm whether any US, EU or AU site is accepting patients for a dual CD33/CD123 construct before considering travel to Shenzhen; at this check none was found

If the family wants the Chinese option explored anyway, have the treating haematologist write to c@szgimi.org about non-resident enrollment, manufacturing timelines and follow-up obligations, and get the cost structure in writing
In the meantime pursue CD33 and CD123 sequentially through reachable agents rather than waiting on a dual construct
Order quantitative CD33 and CD123 density, which any dual-targeting conversation will require
geographic_scope: Mainland China only (Shenzhen, Guangdong). No US, EU or AU site identified.

intervention_label: Lintuzumab-Ac225 (225Ac anti-CD33, Actimab-A) after CLAG-M salvage
regulatory_status: investigational; no FDA or EMA filing

trials.title: Lintuzumab-Ac225 with venetoclax and ASTX-727 in AML
trials.notes: NCI-sponsored; registry reason for suspension reads 'Drug Supply Issues', last updated 2026-05-13. Also written for patients ineligible for induction therapy.

trials.title: Lintuzumab-Ac225 in high-risk MDS after hypomethylating agent failure
trials.notes: NCI-sponsored, suspended for the same recorded reason, last updated 2026-06-24.

trials.title: Lintuzumab-Ac225 with CLAG-M in relapsed/refractory AML
trials.notes: The Medical College of Wisconsin study behind the CLAG-M combination rationale; completed, not a current route.

manufacturer.notes: Actinium's public contact page lists investorrelations@actiniumpharma.com and a New York address but no medical-information or expanded-access line. The nearest verifiable clinical contact is the Actinium medical contact listed on the apamistamab registry record (mvusirikala@actiniumpharma.com, 347-814-2268), which is a trial contact rather than a medical-information desk.

access_summary: Both NCI studies of lintuzumab-Ac225 are suspended with 'Drug Supply Issues' on the registry record, and no restart date is posted. The CLAG-M combination that generated the salvage rationale completed years ago. Until actinium-225 supply is resolved there is nothing to enrol into and no compassionate protocol to request.
next_steps: If the team wants this pursued, ask Actinium's registry medical contact (mvusirikala@actiniumpharma.com) directly whether isotope supply has a restart timeline
Do not build a treatment plan around a suspended isotope programme; keep CLAG-M itself as the transferable part of the rationale
Re-check both NCI records in 8 to 12 weeks, since supply suspensions can lift without an announcement

intervention_label: Rezatapopt (PC14586, TP53 Y220C-selective p53 reactivator)
regulatory_status: investigational; no FDA or EMA approval. Sponsor has stated a planned 2027 US submission in TP53 Y220C-mutant ovarian cancer.

trials.title: Rezatapopt plus azacitidine in TP53 Y220C-mutant AML and MDS
trials.indication: Relapsed or primary refractory AML, or MDS-IB1/IB2
trials.notes: The one haematologic rezatapopt study. Requires a TP53 Y220C mutation confirmed by CLIA-approved local testing at a variant allele frequency above 2%, ECOG <=2, and adequate organ function. Two sites: MD Anderson and Moffitt. Registry updated 2026-07-29, completion estimated 2029-08-27. Everything hangs on the variant-level TP53 readout, which this case has not yet obtained.

trials.title: Rezatapopt with or without pembrolizumab in TP53 Y220C-mutant advanced solid tumours
trials.indication: Locally advanced or metastatic solid tumours
trials.central_contact_name: PMV Pharma Clinical Study Information Center
trials.notes: Solid tumours only, so a haematologic malignancy is out. Listed here because it is the sponsor's main study and the contact point most likely to answer questions about the molecule.

manufacturer.notes: PMV's published access policy states that a treating physician may submit an inquiry or a formal expanded-access request on a patient's behalf by email to clinicaltrials@pmvpharma.com, with each request evaluated case by case.

payer_access_notes: Investigational and sponsor-supplied on study. An expanded-access supply is typically provided at no charge but does not cover the surrounding care.
access_summary: Rezatapopt is only worth pursuing if the TP53 variant turns out to be Y220C, and the trial requires that confirmed on a CLIA assay above 2% variant allele frequency, which this case does not have. The one haematologic study runs at MD Anderson and Moffitt with a named contact. PMV also publishes an expanded-access address, so a Y220C-positive result opens two doors rather than one.
next_steps: Get variant-level TP53 sequencing done on a CLIA assay that reports the specific amino-acid change and the variant allele frequency, and pair it with p53 immunohistochemistry and 17p FISH, since the 2026 panel had a 2% limit of detection and no copy-number calling
If Y220C is confirmed, email Courtney DiNardo's team at MD Anderson (cdinardo@mdanderson.org, NCT06616636) with the report attached
If Y220C is confirmed but no slot exists, have the treating physician submit an expanded-access request to clinicaltrials@pmvpharma.com per PMV's published policy
If the variant is a non-Y220C TP53 aberration, close this line rather than substituting eprenetapopt, which has no live programme
Retrieve the 2019 report's exact variant identity and allele frequency in parallel; it may answer the question without new sequencing
geographic_scope: United States; the haematologic study runs at MD Anderson (Houston, TX) and Moffitt (Tampa, FL).

intervention_label: Eprenetapopt (APR-246) plus venetoclax and azacitidine
regulatory_status: investigational; development discontinued after the phase 3 in TP53-mutant MDS missed its primary endpoint

trials.title: Eprenetapopt plus venetoclax with or without azacitidine in TP53-mutant myeloid malignancies
trials.notes: Completed 2022-01-14; no successor study open.

manufacturer.notes: After the phase 3 miss the company acquired Atrin and moved its focus to DNA-damage-response assets. No current eprenetapopt trials and no expanded-access programme identified.

access_summary: The registrational trial in TP53-mutant MDS failed its primary endpoint and Aprea moved on, so there is no sponsor, no open study and no compassionate route. The upstream read that eprenetapopt is low-yield here matches the access picture. If the TP53 question resolves to Y220C, rezatapopt is the live molecule, not this one.
next_steps: Record eprenetapopt as closed and do not hold it as a TP53 fallback
Direct any confirmed TP53 Y220C result to rezatapopt (NCT06616636) instead
geographic_scope: No open access path in any geography.

intervention_label: Second allogeneic haematopoietic cell transplant (HCT2)
regulatory_status: Established procedure rather than a regulated product; conditioning agents are individually approved, and treosulfan was FDA-approved in the US in 2025 for use in allogeneic transplant conditioning.

trials.title: Decitabine plus FLAG-Ida followed by reduced-intensity conditioning allogeneic HCT
trials.notes: Fred Hutch, single site, registry updated 2026-05-15. Prior TBI-containing allogeneic HCT is permissible up to 3 Gy if more than 6 months after the transplant, so the 2020 regimen again decides eligibility. Sibling donors must be genotypically or phenotypically HLA-identical confirmed by high-resolution typing, which is another reason the pending HLA retrieval is load-bearing. Matched-unrelated, mismatched-unrelated and haploidentical donors are all accommodated. Note the regimen repeats a FLAG-Ida backbone that this patient has already progressed through, which is a clinical rather than an access objection.

trials.title: 211At-BC8-B10 followed by donor stem cell transplant
trials.notes: The radioimmunotherapy-conditioning route to a second transplant; requires a haploidentical related donor and excludes prior myeloablative conditioning.

manufacturer.company: Not applicable; delivered by transplant centres. Donor search and unrelated-donor logistics run through NMDP.
manufacturer.notes: Access runs through a transplant programme's evaluation, not a manufacturer. The relevant contacts are the treating centre's transplant coordinator and the original donor's centre.

payer_access_notes: A second allogeneic transplant is covered by Medicare and most commercial plans as established care for relapsed AML, but it is prior-authorised individually and payers look closely at disease control before conditioning. Refractory disease at roughly 85% marrow blasts is the most likely reason for an authorisation fight, which is an argument for documented cytoreduction first.
access_summary: A second allograft is the platform the rest of the curative-intent plan sits on, and unlike most rows here it needs no trial and no manufacturer. What gates it is disease control and a donor decision, not availability. Two Fred Hutch protocols wrap the transplant in a specific conditioning strategy, and both hinge on what the 2020 conditioning regimen was.
next_steps: Get a transplant-programme consultation booked now rather than after salvage, since donor work-up and authorisation run on a longer clock than chemotherapy
Retrieve the 2020 conditioning regimen and the high-resolution HLA typing for the patient and the sibling, which every transplant protocol here asks for

Ask the transplant team to decide between the original HLA-identical sibling and a haploidentical family donor, since some protocols require the latter and graft-versus-leukaemia escape argues for a different donor
Contact the Fred Hutch DEC-FLAG-Ida study (nali2@fredhutch.org, 206-667-5854, NCT06928662) if a conditioning trial is wanted, and raise the prior FLAG-Ida failure with them directly
Begin payer pre-authorisation early and document the cytoreduction plan, because disease burden is what payers will question
geographic_scope: United States; the transplant itself is available at any allogeneic transplant centre, while the two conditioning protocols are Seattle-only.

intervention_label: 211At-BC8-B10 (astatine-211 anti-CD45) conditioning before allogeneic HCT
regulatory_status: investigational; no filing

trials.title: 211At-BC8-B10 followed by donor stem cell transplant in relapsed/refractory high-risk acute leukaemia and MDS
trials.notes: Single site, Fred Hutchinson Cancer Center; registry updated 2026-06-22, completion estimated 2029-10-20. Three things to check against this case. Prior myeloablative allogeneic HCT is an exclusion, while prior non-myeloablative or reduced-intensity allo-HCT is allowed if there is no ongoing GVHD and the patient has been off all immunosuppression for at least 6 weeks, so the 2020 conditioning regimen decides eligibility. The protocol requires a related donor identical for one HLA haplotype and mismatched at the unshared haplotype, which an HLA-identical sibling is not, so a different family member would have to be the donor. Circulating blasts should be under 10,000/mm3, hydroxyurea allowed. Blasts must express CD45 in patients not in remission.

manufacturer.notes: Academic radiochemistry programme with no commercial sponsor or medical-information line; astatine-211 is produced locally, which is why the study is single-site.

payer_access_notes: The conditioning agent is supplied by the study; the transplant itself is billed as clinical care. A haploidentical second transplant needs prior authorisation in its own right, separate from the trial.
access_summary: This is a live, recruiting radioimmunotherapy-conditioning route at Fred Hutch, and it is the practical replacement for Iomab-B. Two facts about this patient decide it: whether the 2020 transplant used myeloablative conditioning, which would exclude her, and whether a haploidentical family donor exists, since the protocol wants a one-haplotype-mismatched related donor rather than the HLA-identical sibling. Both are answerable from the chart and a family history.
next_steps: Pull the 2020 conditioning regimen from the transplant record and establish whether it was myeloablative, since that single fact opens or closes this option
Map the family for a haploidentical donor (children, parents, other siblings), because the HLA-identical sibling does not meet this protocol's donor requirement
Email Phuong Vo's team (ptvo@fredhutch.org, 206-667-2749, NCT03670966) with the conditioning history and donor picture rather than a general enquiry
Confirm CD45 expression on blasts is documented, and get circulating blasts under 10,000/mm3 with hydroxyurea before screening
Coordinate with the NCT03326921 intake at the same institution, since both routes run through Fred Hutch and could be sequenced
geographic_scope: United States; single site in Seattle, Washington.

intervention_label: 131I-apamistamab (Iomab-B) targeted conditioning before allogeneic HCT
regulatory_status: not approved. The FDA determined that the SIERRA analyses did not adequately support a BLA filing and required an additional randomised study demonstrating an overall-survival benefit (announced August 2024).

trials.title: 131I-apamistamab conditioning with fludarabine/cyclophosphamide/TBI before allogeneic HCT in relapsed/refractory AML
trials.notes: The FDA-requested confirmatory study. Two exclusions close it to this patient: prior allogeneic or autologous HSCT is excluded outright, and marrow blasts must be between 5% and 20%, against roughly 85% here. No sites were listed at the 2025-09-10 registry update and the study is not yet recruiting.

trials.title: SIERRA: Iomab-B conditioning plus allogeneic HCT in relapsed/refractory AML
trials.notes: The pivotal study; closed to enrollment. Its TP53-mutant subgroup is the reason this agent entered the dossier.

manufacturer.notes: No medical-information or expanded-access line is published on Actinium's contact page, which lists investorrelations@actiniumpharma.com and a New York address. The registry medical contact for the new study (mvusirikala@actiniumpharma.com, 347-814-2268) is a trial contact. Actinium and Immedica announced a commercialisation agreement for Iomab-B in Europe, the Middle East and North Africa, which is contingent on an approval that has not happened.

access_summary: Iomab-B has no approval anywhere and the FDA rejected the SIERRA package, asking for a new randomised trial. That trial is not yet recruiting, has no listed sites, excludes anyone with a prior allograft and caps marrow blasts at 20%, so it fails this patient on two independent criteria. Targeted radioimmunotherapy conditioning stays on the table only through the astatine-211 anti-CD45 protocol at Fred Hutch.
next_steps: Treat Iomab-B as unavailable for this case and put the radioimmunotherapy-conditioning question to NCT03670966 (211At-BC8-B10) instead
If confirmation is wanted, email mvusirikala@actiniumpharma.com asking whether any prior-transplant cohort is planned for the new study
Do not delay a second-transplant decision waiting for this programme, which is years from any approval
geographic_scope: No accessible path; the sponsor's new study has no listed sites and the European commercialisation agreement is contingent on a future approval.

intervention_label: FLAMSA-RIC (sequential fludarabine/cytarabine/amsacrine with reduced-intensity conditioning and prophylactic DLI)
regulatory_status: Sequential-conditioning strategy assembled from individually approved agents. Amsacrine is not FDA-approved in the United States, which is why US centres substitute other sequential regimens.

trials.title: Venetoclax plus FLAMSA and treosulfan conditioning before allogeneic HCT
trials.notes: Six German sites, registry last updated 2024-05-01. The registry lists extension 826 for the contact phone. Venetoclax-containing conditioning against documented venetoclax refractoriness is a clinical objection worth putting to the investigator. Germany-only.

trials.title: Decitabine plus FLAG-Ida followed by reduced-intensity conditioning allogeneic HCT
trials.notes: The reachable US expression of the same sequential-conditioning idea: cytoreduction immediately followed by reduced-intensity conditioning and transplant.

manufacturer.company: Not applicable; investigator-directed conditioning strategy using marketed agents
manufacturer.notes: No single manufacturer. Amsacrine's absence from the US market is the practical reason FLAMSA proper is rarely delivered in the United States.

payer_access_notes: Delivered as part of a transplant admission and authorised with the transplant rather than separately. Agent-level coverage is not usually the obstacle; the transplant authorisation is.
access_summary: FLAMSA-RIC in its original form is hard to reproduce in the United States because amsacrine is not marketed here, and the one recruiting FLAMSA study is in Germany with a venetoclax-containing arm that sits awkwardly against documented venetoclax refractoriness. The transferable idea, cytoreduction running straight into reduced-intensity conditioning, is available in the US through the Fred Hutch DEC-FLAG-Ida protocol or as an institutional sequential regimen. Discuss it as a conditioning strategy with the transplant team rather than as a drug to obtain.
next_steps: Raise sequential conditioning with the transplant programme as a strategy question and ask what their institutional sequential regimen is, given amsacrine is not available in the US
If the German study is of interest, email Guido Kobbe (kobbe@med.uni-duesseldorf.de, NCT05807932) and ask about non-resident enrollment and about the venetoclax arm in a venetoclax-refractory patient
Consider NCT06928662 at Fred Hutch as the US-reachable equivalent, subject to the prior-TBI and 6-month conditions
Fold prophylactic post-transplant DLI planning into the conditioning discussion, since it is part of what makes the sequential approach work
geographic_scope: Germany for the FLAMSA study; the sequential-conditioning strategy is deliverable at US transplant centres in modified form.

intervention_label: Donor lymphocyte infusion (DLI) from the HLA-identical sibling donor
regulatory_status: Established post-transplant practice; cells are collected and infused under the transplant programme's own authorisations rather than as a licensed product.

trials.title: Interferon gamma-1b plus donor leukocyte infusion for AML relapse after allogeneic HCT
trials.notes: Three sites: Washington University, UPMC Hillman and Fred Hutch. Sponsor of record is Sawa Ito, MD at UPMC Hillman. Blast criteria close it at present disease burden: at least 5% myeloblasts by morphology but not exceeding 30%, and abnormal cells with a leukaemia-associated immunophenotype not exceeding 30% of nucleated cells. It becomes reachable if salvage brings blasts down. Second registry contact: Amy Rodger, RN, 412-623-4036, rodgax@upmc.edu. Registry updated 2026-07-30.

manufacturer.company: Not applicable; cells come from the original sibling donor via the transplant centre's collection facility
manufacturer.notes: The only access dependency is the donor's willingness and fitness to donate again, plus the original transplant centre's ability to release or re-collect donor cells.

payer_access_notes: DLI after allogeneic transplant is routinely covered as established care for post-transplant relapse. Costs are the collection, the infusion and the management of any resulting GVHD, all billed through the transplant programme.
access_summary: DLI is one of the few options in this dossier the patient's own team can arrange without a sponsor, a trial slot or an off-label appeal, since the sibling donor is identified and the relapse pattern points to graft-versus-leukaemia escape rather than graft failure. Its weakness is disease burden, because DLI works poorly against bulky disease and is usually given after cytoreduction. The interferon-gamma combination study would add to it but caps blasts at 30%.
next_steps: Ask the original transplant centre what donor cells are still available and whether the sibling would consent to a fresh collection, since that answer takes time to obtain
Sequence DLI after cytoreduction rather than against 85% marrow blasts, which is both the clinical and the trial-eligibility position
If salvage brings blasts under 30%, contact the UPMC study team (eliaslj@upmc.edu, 412-623-6037, NCT06529731) about the interferon gamma-1b plus DLI protocol
Discuss GVHD risk explicitly with the patient, since a six-year disease-free interval suggests a tolerated graft that DLI would deliberately provoke
Ask the transplant team about class II HLA downregulation on the relapsed blasts, which is the mechanism most likely to blunt a DLI response after an HLA-identical sibling graft
geographic_scope: United States; DLI itself is available at any transplant centre, the combination study at three sites (St Louis, Pittsburgh, Seattle).

intervention_label: Revumenib (SNDX-5613, menin inhibitor)
regulatory_status: FDA-approved as REVUFORJ for relapsed or refractory acute leukaemia with a KMT2A translocation (November 2024) and for relapsed or refractory NPM1-mutated AML in adult and paediatric patients 1 year and older (October 2025).
guideline_status: NCCN guidelines list revumenib for relapsed/refractory NPM1-mutated AML. No listing for KMT2A amplification without a translocation.

manufacturer.notes: Syndax publishes medinfo@syndax.com and 1-888-539-3REV (3738) for medical information and adverse-event reporting. SyndAccess is the company's patient-support and reimbursement programme.

payer_access_notes: On-label use is reimbursed against a KMT2A translocation or an NPM1 mutation. Neither applies here: the 2026 cytogenetics show KMT2A amplification with four copies, which is not a rearrangement, and no NPM1 mutation has been reported. An off-label request without either lesion has no compendia support and should be expected to fail.
access_summary: Revumenib is approved and easy to obtain, which makes it tempting, but the label and the biology both turn on a KMT2A translocation or an NPM1 mutation and this patient has neither. KMT2A amplification is a different lesion and does not create menin dependence. The clinician logged it as out of scope for the same reason, and the access answer does not change that.
next_steps: Do not pursue revumenib on the basis of KMT2A amplification; confirm with the treating haematologist that no KMT2A rearrangement was seen on the relapse karyotype
If a full metaphase karyotype at relapse does turn up a KMT2A translocation, the drug becomes on-label and Syndax medical information (medinfo@syndax.com, 1-888-539-3REV) is the contact
Re-test NPM1 at relapse if it has not been done, since clonal evolution could open the second label
geographic_scope: United States; approved and commercially available.

intervention_label: Venetoclax (BCL-2 inhibition) — prior exposure and TP53-dependent resistance
regulatory_status: FDA-approved (VENCLEXTA) including for newly-diagnosed AML in adults 75 or older or unfit for intensive induction, in combination with azacitidine, decitabine or low-dose cytarabine. No approved indication in relapsed or refractory AML.

manufacturer.company: AbbVie and Genentech (co-marketed in the United States)
manufacturer.notes: (800) 821-8590 is the Genentech medical information line, Monday to Friday 5 am to 5 pm PT. AbbVie medical information is 844-663-3742. Genentech's adverse-event line is (888) 835-2555.

payer_access_notes: On-label use is in newly-diagnosed AML in unfit adults; relapsed/refractory use is off-label and, in a patient already documented as refractory to a venetoclax-containing regimen, hard to justify to a payer or to a treating team.
access_summary: Venetoclax is easy to get and that is not the issue: this patient progressed through FLAG-IDA plus venetoclax, and TP53 aberration is the canonical driver of BCL-2-inhibitor resistance. The reason this row exists is sequencing rather than acquisition, because several trials on the list carry venetoclax-containing arms that would repeat an exposure she has already failed. Raise that with any investigator before consenting to such an arm.
next_steps: When screening trials, check whether the assigned arm contains venetoclax and put the documented refractoriness to the investigator before consenting
Do not plan venetoclax re-challenge as monotherapy or with a hypomethylating agent alone on the strength of availability
If a mechanistically different combination is proposed, ask what evidence supports re-sensitisation in a TP53-aberrant, previously exposed patient
geographic_scope: United States and EU; widely available.

intervention_label: Extramedullary myeloid sarcoma (right thigh) — assessment and local control
regulatory_status: Not a drug. Biopsy, cross-sectional imaging and local radiotherapy are established clinical services rather than regulated products.

manufacturer.notes: No manufacturer. Access runs through the treating centre's interventional radiology, pathology and radiation oncology services.

payer_access_notes: Biopsy, MRI and palliative or consolidative radiotherapy to a symptomatic myeloid sarcoma are routinely covered. The item most likely to need justification is repeat cross-sectional imaging for response assessment at a site outside the marrow.
access_summary: This row is biology rather than a drug, and it earns a place because the thigh lesion changes what the other options can achieve. A sanctuary site can carry a different clone from the marrow, so a biopsy of the lesion is the only way to know whether CD33 and CD123 are expressed there at the density the marrow shows. Every trial screening in this dossier will also ask for current extramedullary disease measurements.
next_steps: Ask whether the thigh lesion can be biopsied for site-specific immunophenotype and genotype rather than assuming the marrow result applies to it
Include the lesion in baseline imaging so response can be assessed separately from the marrow, since trials will ask for it
Raise local radiotherapy with radiation oncology for symptom control or consolidation, particularly if a systemic response leaves the thigh lesion behind
Flag the extramedullary site to any cell-therapy or engager investigator, since trafficking to soft-tissue disease is a known weak point of those modalities
geographic_scope: Available at the treating centre; no geographic constraint.
